title: Sole Trader vs Partnership Adventure
welcome_lead: One owner or two? Meet the two simplest business types. 🤝
meta_desc: Types of Business Adventure 1 — KS3 Business Studies on sole traders and partnerships.
final_note: You learned what a sole trader and a partnership are, and how they compare.

concepts.def: One person who owns the business
2+ people who own a business together
Owner is liable for all debts

walkthroughs.body_html:
A sole trader is one self-employed person.

Examples: a window cleaner, a hairdresser, a market trader.

Pros: easy to start, you keep all profit.
Cons: unlimited liability — your home could pay business debts. 😬

A partnership is 2–20 owners working together.

Examples: a vet practice, a law firm.

Partners share workload, ideas and profit — but also debts.

Compare:

  • Sole trader — full control, full risk.
  • Partnership — shared brain, shared debt.

A good deed of partnership writes down who does what and how profit is split. 📜

mcqs.q: What is a key disadvantage of being a sole trader?
options: Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
The main disadvantage is that sole traders can't sell any products.
Unlimited liability — the owner's personal assets are at risk if the business fails, because there is no legal separation between owner and business.
Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.

mcqs.q: Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.
The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.
